docs.title: DeadlineDesk
docs.text:
UCS503P Software Engineering, Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology.

DeadlineDesk combines placement-round readiness and academic assignment deadlines. Placement administrators publish rounds and required checklists. Students track readiness and submit academic work. The assignment's TA applies a published late policy, reviews accepted work and publishes grades and feedback.

Team: Aryan Gupta (1024030764), Aksh Goyal (1024030766), Naveen Bansal (1024030767).

Final evaluation: Tuesday, 1 December 2026, 8:00 AM, Lab 105.

docs.title: Final submission
docs.text:
Deliverable Open Final report, LaTeX and PDF Report Final presentation and inline slides Presentation Eight UML diagram types Individual diagram folders Gantt chart PDF and preview Test cases Catalogue and recorded results Individual journals Team journal index Working application Public demo and startup guide Verification Application, browser and publication evidence All deliverables, including proposal and prototype Complete submission index

The final presentation covers Introduction, Background, Problem Statement, Your Solution, and Results in that order. The report includes a dedicated design and evaluation section containing all eight UML diagrams, the Gantt chart and the complete test-case catalogue.

docs.title: Architecture and workflows
docs.text:
The frontend uses Django HTML templates and CSS. Python views, forms and services implement the backend. Django's ORM stores structured records in SQLite, while private uploads use a local media directory. Session authentication, CSRF protection, role checks and assignment ownership checks protect the workflows.

The placement workflow is company and draft round creation, required checklist definition, publication, reminder-log persistence and student readiness. The academic workflow is assignment publication, validated upload, server-time late-policy decision, review, grading and student feedback.

See the architecture and design, SRS, current backlog and final demo guide.

GitHub Pages serves these documents and previews. The Python application runs separately at the temporary public demo linked above. Its host and HTTPS tunnel must stay running.

docs.title: Scope decisions
docs.text:
The announcement specifies eight UML diagrams without naming their types. The submission uses use-case, class, sequence, activity, state-machine, component, deployment and package diagrams. DFD, ER and Gantt diagrams are separate supporting diagrams.

Keep historical Week 4 and Week 7 artifacts. Add final artifacts once and link to their canonical files. Preserve weekly journals rather than inventing unrecorded work for intervening weeks. Current limitations include logged reminders without delivery, a token-overlap similarity stub, SQLite/local file storage and no malware scanning.

docs.title: 1. Frame the problem (30 seconds)
docs.text: Placement and academic deadlines currently arrive through disconnected channels. DeadlineDesk proves that both workflows can share authentication, policy decisions, status history, and audit evidence.

docs.title: 2. Placement Admin path (90 seconds)
docs.text:
Sign in as placement / Placement@W7.

  1. Open Placement and show the sample company/round.
  2. Explain draft versus effective published/open/closed state.
  3. Show the required document checklist.
  4. Show the T-24h reminder log created at publish time.

docs.title: 3. Student placement path (60 seconds)
docs.text:
Sign in as student / Student@W7.

  1. Open the published Northstar Systems round.
  2. Toggle each required document.
  3. Show the readiness result change to "Ready to apply."

docs.title: 4. Academic path (150 seconds)
docs.text:
Sign in as ta / Faculty@W7 and show the assignment plus its grace-window policy. Then sign in as Student.

  1. Open the assignment and point out the authoritative due time.
  2. Upload a small text file.
  3. Show submitted time, late decision, penalty, and similarity-stub warning.
  4. Return as TA, start review, and publish a score/feedback.
  5. Return as Student and show the grade.

docs.title: 5. Engineering evidence (60 seconds)
docs.text: Run the test suite. Explain the six late-policy boundary tests, authorization test, reminder test, checklist test, and full submission-to-grade integration test.

docs.title: 6. Scope honesty (30 seconds)
docs.text: State clearly: reminders are database logs, similarity is simple text-token overlap, and SQLite/local files are prototype choices. Week 8 prioritizes authorization hardening and staging deployment.

docs.title: Likely viva questions
docs.text:
Why Django? It provides mature authentication, CSRF, ORM migrations, forms, file handling, and testing, which reduces Week 7 integration risk.

Why not combine late status with submission state? Review status and late outcome are independent. A late submission can still move from submitted to reviewed to graded.

What happens exactly at the deadline? submitted_at <= due_at is on time. The boundary is covered by an automated test.

Is the similarity score plagiarism detection? No. It is a labeled Jaccard token-overlap stub for text and returns 0 for unsupported content.

How will email be added? A retry-safe worker will consume scheduled ReminderLog rows and record sent time without changing the round-publishing transaction.

What is the main security gap? The prototype TA role is global. Production must scope staff actions to their assigned courses or sections.

docs.title: Architectural view
docs.text:
DeadlineDesk uses Django's layered monolith pattern. The final submission preserves the Week 7 workflow baseline and adds ownership/privacy guards and deployment tooling.

Browser
  -> URL router and role-protected views
      -> Forms and application services
          -> Domain models and policy decisions
              -> Django ORM
                  -> SQLite database and local media

This shape keeps deployment simple while preserving boundaries that can later support PostgreSQL, background workers, or an API frontend.

The public application demo runs separately from the GitHub Pages documentation. Gunicorn serves Django with debug disabled; WhiteNoise serves collected static files, and a temporary HTTPS tunnel forwards requests to the application host. SQLite and private media live in an isolated demonstration directory. The host and tunnel must remain active for the temporary URL to work.

docs.text:
Placement Admin -> Create company -> Create draft round

docs.text:
TA -> Publish assignment and late policy
Student -> Upload file
System -> Timestamp -> Evaluate policy -> Similarity stub -> Persist submission

docs.title: Placement round
docs.text:
draft -> published -> open -> closed -> archived

open and closed are calculated from the published round's timestamps. Draft and archived remain explicit states.

docs.title: Submission
docs.text:
submitted -> under_review -> graded

Late outcome is an orthogonal attribute: on_time, grace, or penalty. A rejected attempt creates no submission.

docs.title: Domain model
docs.text: Entity Important relationships / constraints User Role is Student, TA, or Placement Admin Company Created by Placement Admin; has many rounds PlacementRound Belongs to Company; has checklist items and reminder logs ChecklistItem Required/optional and ordered within a round ChecklistCompletion Unique for one Student and one ChecklistItem ReminderLog Belongs to a round; scheduled/sent status Assignment Created by TA; due time and one late-policy configuration Submission Unique for one Student and one Assignment; owns uploaded file Grade One-to-one with Submission AuditLog Actor plus action and generic entity reference

docs.title: Design diagrams
docs.text:
Editable draw.io sources and their PDF/PNG exports live in project-proposal/figures/, and the submission pages show them inline:

  • Use-case diagram
  • Data-flow diagrams, Levels 0 and 1
  • Gantt chart, activity diagrams, ER model, class diagram and sequence diagrams

make diagrams re-exports every PDF and PNG from the .drawio sources. See Repository structure for the full workflow.

docs.title: Django and server-rendered pages
docs.text: Django was selected because the prototype needs secure sessions, role guards, forms, file uploads, persistence, migrations, and tests more than it needs frontend framework complexity. Server rendering reduces integration risk for the Week 7 demonstration.

docs.title: SQLite now, PostgreSQL later
docs.text: SQLite makes setup deterministic for evaluators. The application uses the ORM and avoids SQLite-specific queries, so later migration to PostgreSQL is straightforward.

docs.title: Similarity as an explicit stub
docs.text: The system reads each file as UTF-8 and ignores bytes it cannot decode, then computes the maximum Jaccard overlap of lowercase tokens (three or more letters, digits or underscores) against earlier submissions to the same assignment. An empty token set scores 0. Because undecodable bytes are skipped rather than rejected, a binary file such as a PDF can still produce a small non-zero score, so the number is only meaningful for text files. The UI explicitly warns that this is not a plagiarism verdict.

docs.title: Reminder database-first design
docs.text: Publishing stores the intended T-24h delivery record. A future background worker can consume scheduled rows and send email without changing the placement workflow.

docs.title: Security controls and known gaps
docs.text:
Implemented controls: password hashing, CSRF, session authentication, route-level authorization, server validation, upload size/type limits, unique database constraints, and transactional publish/grade flows.

Final ownership checks restrict TA assignment lists, rosters, pending submissions, review, grading and academic file access to assignments created by that TA. A Student can view/download only their own submission, and Placement Admin cannot access private academic submissions. Dashboard activity is scoped to its current user. Checklist changes require the round's effective status to be open. These guards are covered by the final test catalogue.

The final demo runner supplies a random runtime secret when none is configured and disables debug mode. Settings reject debug-disabled startup without an explicit secret. The ordinary development defaults remain available for local development, so a permanent host must configure its environment deliberately.

Remaining gaps: no malware scanning, no rate limiting, no email verification or reminder delivery, no managed object storage, no institutional course/section model and no concurrency qualification on PostgreSQL. Assignment-owner checks are implemented; course-section membership is future work. The temporary single-host demo is not a durable production service.

docs.title: Final artifact workflow
docs.text:
The eight UML types each have their own folder under docs/uml/, with editable draw.io source and PDF/PNG exports. Detailed Week 7 diagrams remain in project-proposal/figures/. Final use-case, class and activity revisions have their own sources to document the new guards; the unchanged submission sequence is shared through relative symlinks. State, component, deployment and package sources live in their final UML folders. DFD and ER diagrams remain supporting material outside the count of eight UML types.

scripts/export_diagrams.py exports both baseline and final sources without rewriting them. The preparation script creates missing final sources once and leaves existing editable sources intact. The final report embeds all eight UML types, the final Gantt chart and the test cases. See the submission checklist and verification record for completion evidence.

docs.title: Final application and artifact verification
docs.text: Verified on 25 November 2026 against the final-submission working tree. The public demo uses synthetic data, Gunicorn 23.0.0, Django 5.2.5 and Python 3.12 with debug disabled. GitHub Actions records the checks for the published commit.

docs.title: Automated verification
docs.text:
36 cases passed, zero failed. The test-case catalogue records each parameterized case, its steps, expected result and observed pass. Tests use isolated databases and temporary media rather than the normal development database.

python -m pytest -q --tb=short --junitxml=tmp/final-qa/junit.xml
python code/manage.py check
python code/manage.py makemigrations --check
python code/manage.py collectstatic --noinput
python -m mkdocs build --strict

The suite covers six late-policy boundaries, placement publication/reminders, student checklist changes, upload-to-grade integration, private downloads, twelve unrelated-user route combinations, four non-open checklist states, current-user audit feeds, TA roster ownership, invalid uploads, CSRF/login/logout, duplicate/grade preservation and repeated demo seeding.

docs.title: Public HTTPS browser walkthrough
docs.text:
The browser exercised the running temporary application, not only a Django test client.

Check Observed result Incorrect password Sign-in form showed an error and stayed unauthenticated. Student, TA and Placement Admin sign-in Each reached its corresponding dashboard. POST sign-out returned to sign-in. Placement Admin company and round creation A synthetic company and draft round persisted. Publish without required item Form feedback requested a required checklist item; round stayed draft. Add item and publish Round became Open and a T-24h reminder record appeared. Student checklist Completing every required item changed the result to Ready to apply. TA assignment publication Missing grace duration showed a validation error; entering 60 minutes published the assignment and displayed its policy. Student real file upload A synthetic source-code file produced an accepted on-time submission with a server timestamp and labeled similarity stub. TA review Status changed from Submitted to Under review. Invalid score 101/100 showed Score cannot exceed the maximum score and did not publish a grade. Valid grade 92/100 and feedback persisted. The student saw the same result after a fresh sign-in. Authenticated download The student's download completed. The automated test also verifies exact original file bytes. Placement Admin opens academic submission Custom 403 Access denied page. Student opens company-create route Custom 403 Access denied page. Console Zero captured application console errors or warnings during the reviewed workflows.

docs.title: Responsive regression
docs.text:
A long submitted filename initially caused horizontal overflow on a narrow screen. The fix gives grid children a zero minimum width and wraps long file links and feedback. The final browser check measured 325 CSS pixels for both viewport and document width on the narrow view, and 1200 CSS pixels for both on the desktop view. No horizontal document overflow remained on the submission page. This is a targeted responsive check, not an accessibility certification.

The measurements came from the browser's actual CSS viewport and document dimensions, rather than the requested device preset. Browser screenshot exports were clipped by the capture surface's scaling, so those captures are retained privately and are not used as published layout evidence.

docs.title: Document and diagram checks
docs.text:
The final report compiles from LaTeX and includes its dedicated section containing eight UML types, Gantt chart and all test cases. Each UML folder supplies editable draw.io XML, a one-page PDF and PNG. Diagram review checked labels, edge routing, unique XML IDs and valid edge references. Historical milestone sources remain available.

The final presentation has 16 slides in the instructor's five-section order: Introduction, Background, Problem Statement, Your Solution, Results. Its editable PowerPoint passed package, layout and font validation and a first-party import check. All slides were visually inspected. PDF conversion used LibreOffice after the authoring runtime's native PDF export was unavailable; the resulting PDF has searchable text. No PowerPoint-native visual verification is claimed.

The application changes also received an independent source review focused on private records, ownership checks, CSRF, debug-off startup, static files and the synthetic deployment. No concrete blocking defect was found within that review scope.

docs.title: Published verification
docs.text:
The application/artifact revision b766877 passed application CI and the strict MkDocs build and publish job. The subsequent GitHub Pages deployment succeeded.

After publication, 50 live pages and assets were checked: the home/submission/UML/demo/test/presentation pages, all eight UML pages with their PDF/PNG exports, the report/test/Gantt/presentation PDFs and all 16 slide previews. The downloaded PDF and PNG bytes matched the checked local artifacts. The running Django login endpoint also returned HTTP 200. These checks establish the recorded publication state, while the temporary demonstration still depends on its host and tunnel.

docs.title: Limits and demonstration lifetime
docs.text:
The public endpoint is a temporary tunnel and requires this host, Gunicorn and the tunnel process to remain active. Restarting the tunnel changes its URL. Reopen the live link before evaluation and follow the startup guide if it has expired. The Dockerfile is supplied for persistent hosting but has not been built or deployed in this verification.

No claim is made for production uptime, malware detection, institutional SSO, external reminder delivery, high load or PostgreSQL concurrency. Similarity remains a token-overlap teaching stub. Test passes and a working demonstration do not remove those boundaries.

docs.title: Start the demonstration
docs.text:
Install Python 3.11 or newer and the repository requirements. From the repository root:

python3 -m venv .venv
./.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
./.venv/bin/python scripts/run_demo.py

The runner disables debug mode, persists a random runtime secret in the ignored .demo-runtime/secret.key with owner-only file permissions when none is configured, uses .demo-runtime/demo.sqlite3 and .demo-runtime/media, applies migrations, collects static assets, seeds the synthetic accounts and starts Gunicorn on http://127.0.0.1:8000/. It does not modify the normal development database. Rerunning the seed refreshes the synthetic round/assignment windows and demo account passwords without adding another scheduled reminder. HTTPS cookies are enabled by default. For a local HTTP-only walkthrough, set DEADLINEDESK_SECURE_COOKIES=0 before launching the runner.

In a separate terminal, with the installed official cloudflared CLI:

cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --protocol http2 --no-autoupdate

Open the HTTPS URL printed by the tunnel, check sign-in from another browser/device and update this page with that URL. Keep both terminals and the host running. Close the tunnel process to stop public access. The active preparation environment uses .venv-submit/; a new checkout may use the .venv/ commands above.

docs.title: Live walkthrough
docs.text:
1. Sign in as Placement Admin. Create a company and draft round with an opening time before now and a future closing time. Add a required checklist item and publish. Show the T-24h reminder record.
  2. Sign out and sign in as Student. Open that round, complete the required items and show Ready to apply. Explain that changes are rejected outside the open window.
  3. Sign in as TA. Publish an assignment with a due time and late policy.
  4. As Student, upload a small synthetic text file. Show the accepted timestamp, late result and similarity stub label.
  5. As the assignment's TA, start review and publish a valid score and feedback. As Student, open the result and download the same submitted file.
  6. Demonstrate a role denial and an invalid form. Open the test-case catalogue for deterministic deadline boundaries and ownership checks.

docs.title: Persistent hosting option
docs.text:
The repository Dockerfile supports a permanent host. Configure a strong DEADLINEDESK_SECRET_KEY, explicit DEADLINEDESK_ALLOWED_HOSTS, the HTTPS origin in DEADLINEDESK_CSRF_ORIGINS, and secure cookies for an HTTPS deployment. Mount durable storage at /data for SQLite and private media, and configure trusted-proxy behavior only behind the intended reverse proxy. The image applies migrations and runs Gunicorn. Create demo accounts explicitly with python code/manage.py seed_demo only on a synthetic demonstration deployment.

The temporary tunnel is the preparation demo. A Dockerfile alone is not evidence of a permanent deployed service.

docs.title: Repository structure
docs.text:
DeadlineDesk keeps implementation, documentation, and submission artifacts separate so each file has one obvious home.

assets/                         Shared TIET branding and static assets
code/                           Django application, migrations, templates, tests
docs/                           MkDocs source: SRS, design, testing, demo and backlog
docs/submission/                Final evaluation index and preserved milestone artifacts
docs/uml/<type>/                Eight UML types, each in its own folder
docs/gantt-chart/               Final Gantt chart source, PDF and PNG
docs/test-cases/                Test-case LaTeX, PDF and recorded results
journals/<roll>-<name>/         Canonical weekly journals and consolidated journal.md
project-proposal/               Updated proposal source, figures and PDF (through Week 7)
project-report-prototype-stage/ Editable Week 7 report source and compiled PDF
project-report-final/           Final report source and compiled PDF
scripts/                        Demo runner and artifact preparation/export scripts

The docs/submission/ folder is an evaluation index. Root folders remain the canonical locations for code, proposal, reports and journals. Relative symlinks and links expose existing artifacts without maintaining duplicate editable copies. The final presentation is canonical in its own submission folder.

docs.title: Diagram sources and exports
docs.text:
Each diagram has one editable .drawio source with matching PDF/PNG exports. Baseline sources remain in project-proposal/figures/. Final use-case, class and activity revisions have their own sources because they document the final ownership and timing guards. The unchanged submission sequence is shared by relative symlink. State-machine, component, deployment and package diagrams live in their individual docs/uml/ folders, and the final schedule lives in docs/gantt-chart/. DFD and ER diagrams are supporting material outside the eight UML types.

  1. Edit the .drawio file in draw.io (desktop or app.diagrams.net).
  2. Run python scripts/export_diagrams.py. It calls draw.io Desktop's CLI to export baseline and final sources, resolving symlinks so a shared source is exported once.
  3. Rebuild affected LaTeX reports from their source directory, for example cd project-report-final && tectonic main.tex.

The export script never writes .drawio sources. scripts/prepare_final_diagrams.py creates missing final source files once; rerunning it preserves existing editable sources. The earlier baseline generators (render_diagrams.py, render_additional_diagrams.py) remain retired because they overwrote edited layouts.

docs.title: Report, test and demonstration state
docs.text:
The final report embeds canonical diagram PDFs and docs/test-cases/catalog.tex. The test catalogue is generated from a real passing pytest JUnit result using scripts/build_test_catalog.py. Re-run tests before regenerating it; a failed run must not produce passing evidence.

The normal local database and the .demo-runtime/ synthetic demonstration database are separate. Runtime data, private uploads and temporary build files are ignored by Git. Demo startup and public-link lifetime and final verification document the application separately from GitHub Pages publication.

docs.title: Software Requirements Specification
docs.text: Product: DeadlineDesk Version: Week 7 prototype, 0.1 Date: 25 August 2026

docs.title: Purpose and scope
docs.text: DeadlineDesk provides one authenticated system for two campus deadline workflows: placement-round readiness and academic assignment submission. The Week 7 scope is intentionally thin but end-to-end. Email reminders, production hosting, PostgreSQL, analytics dashboards, and advanced similarity detection are outside this increment.

docs.title: Stakeholders and actors
docs.text: Actor Goal Authorized actions Student Meet deadlines and see outcomes View published rounds and assignments, complete checklist items, upload one submission, view late status and grade TA / Faculty Apply academic policy consistently Publish assignments, inspect submissions, start review, publish score and feedback Placement Admin Publish structured placement windows Create companies/rounds/checklists, publish rounds, inspect reminder logs Course evaluator Verify software-engineering evidence Run tests, inspect CI, follow demo script, trace requirements to tests

docs.title: Functional requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Week 7 acceptance criterion FR-AUTH-01 The system shall authenticate users with a server-side session. Valid demo credentials open the matching portal; invalid credentials do not authenticate. FR-AUTH-02 The system shall enforce Student, TA, and Placement Admin permissions. A Student request to an admin-only creation page returns HTTP 403. FR-PL-01 A Placement Admin shall create companies and placement rounds. A round persists with opening, closing, and draft status. FR-PL-02 A Placement Admin shall add required or optional checklist items. Items appear in the round in configured order. FR-PL-03 Publishing a round shall expose it to students. A published round is listed for Student users; drafts are hidden. FR-PL-04 Publishing shall persist a T-24h reminder record. Reminder time equals closing time minus 24 hours. FR-PL-05 A Student shall toggle checklist completion. Completion is unique per student/item and readiness becomes true when all required items are complete. FR-AC-01 A TA shall publish an assignment with a due time and late policy. Assignment is visible with reject, penalty, or grace configuration. FR-AC-02 A Student shall upload one file per assignment. Accepted file is stored with server submission timestamp. FR-AC-03 The system shall evaluate lateness automatically. Boundary tests agree with the configured policy for exact deadline, rejection, penalty, and grace cases. FR-AC-04 The system shall calculate an explicit similarity stub. Text uploads receive maximum Jaccard token overlap against earlier submissions; unsupported content returns 0. FR-AC-05 A TA shall review and grade a submission. Status becomes graded and the Student sees score and feedback. FR-AUD-01 The system shall persist important domain actions. Audit rows record actor, action, entity, detail, and timestamp.

docs.title: Late-policy rules
docs.text:
Let t be the server submission timestamp and d be the assignment due time.

Policy Decision Any policy, t <= d Accept as on time; penalty 0% Reject, t > d Reject; do not create a submission Accept with penalty, t > d Accept as late; apply configured percentage Grace window, d < t <= d + grace Accept in grace; penalty 0% Grace window, t > d + grace Reject; do not create a submission

The server timestamp is authoritative. Browser time is not used for the decision.

docs.title: Non-functional requirements
docs.text: ID Requirement Measure NFR-SEC-01 State-changing browser requests shall use CSRF protection. Django CSRF middleware and form tokens enabled. NFR-SEC-02 Passwords shall never be stored in plaintext. Django password hashers used through set_password / create_user. NFR-SEC-03 Student uploads shall be accessible only to the owner and staff roles. Files are served through an authenticated download view; cross-student access returns HTTP 403. NFR-REL-01 The fixed late-policy suite shall have 100% agreement. Six of six late-policy tests pass. NFR-MNT-01 Domain decisions shall be isolated from request rendering. Late evaluation and similarity stub live in core/services.py. NFR-ACC-01 Core flows shall be keyboard accessible. Semantic labels, visible focus, skip link, native controls, and contrast-aware themes. NFR-RSP-01 Pages shall support phone and desktop widths. Browser QA at default width and 390 px without horizontal content loss. NFR-OPS-01 Every push shall run build checks and tests. GitHub Actions application CI.

docs.title: Data and retention
docs.text: The prototype uses SQLite and local media storage. Uploaded files are limited to 5 MB and selected academic/source/archive extensions. No automated deletion policy is implemented in Week 7. Production use requires managed storage, malware scanning, retention rules, backups, and privacy approval.

docs.title: Assumptions and constraints
docs.text:
• One active submission per student per assignment.
  • Placement reminder delivery is a database log only.
  • A TA may grade any academic submission in the prototype.
  • Staff accounts are simulated for the pilot.
  • All displayed deadline times use Asia/Kolkata.

docs.title: Browser QA
docs.text:
The prototype was exercised again in an isolated local browser session on 1 September 2026.

docs.title: Reading the diagram
docs.text:
• The rectangle is the DeadlineDesk system boundary; the three stick figures are the actors outside it.
  • Ovals are coloured by the actor that owns the use case: blue for Student, green for TA / Faculty, amber for Placement Admin.

docs.title: Reading the diagrams
docs.text:
• Rectangles are external entities, ovals are processes, and open-ended rectangles are data stores.
  • Arrows describe data movement, not interface navigation or execution order.
  • Level 1 reads left to right: external entity, then process, then data store. An entity marked * is drawn a second time to avoid crossing lines.
  • The two levels are balanced: every flow between an external role and DeadlineDesk in Level 0 appears in Level 1 between that role and one of the processes.
  • There is no email or other external service. The T-24h reminder is a row in D2, and the audit trail is D8.

docs.title: Planning and model diagrams
docs.text:
The diagram sources are editable in diagrams.net / Draw.io. The canonical source files and their PDF/PNG previews live together in project-proposal/figures/; this index links to them rather than storing a second copy.

Diagram Editable Draw.io source PDF preview PNG preview Project Gantt chart, Weeks 3–7 gantt-chart.drawio PDF PNG Placement Track activity activity-placement.drawio PDF PNG Academic Dropbox activity activity-academic.drawio PDF PNG Django entity-relationship (ER) model er-diagram.drawio PDF PNG UML class diagram class-diagram.drawio PDF PNG Sequence: sign-in and role-based access sequence-authentication.drawio PDF PNG Sequence: Placement Admin publishes a round sequence-placement-publish.drawio PDF PNG Sequence: student views a round and completes checklist items sequence-placement-readiness.drawio PDF PNG Sequence: student submits an assignment sequence-submission.drawio PDF PNG Sequence: TA reviews and grades a submission sequence-review-grade.drawio PDF PNG
  • ER model. Taken from code/core/models.py and migrations/0001_initial.py. It shows every foreign key, including the four User links (created_by, student, graded_by, actor), the two unique-together constraints, and the one-to-one Grade. AuditLog.entity_id is a generic reference, not a foreign key.
  • Activity diagrams. UML swimlanes for each role and the system. Each decision matches a branch in the views and forms: publishing needs at least one required item; a submission is rejected if it is a duplicate or blocked by the late policy; uploads must be at most 5 MB and an allowed type; the score cannot exceed the maximum.
  • Gantt chart. Week-level only. Weeks 4–7 come from the team journals; Week 3 is reconstructed from the proposal's combined W3–W4 row and drawn dashed. It makes no day-level estimates.
  • Class diagram. Shows the Week 7 code in code/core: the ten models with their fields, enumerations and foreign-key associations, plus the views, forms, services and decorators. Views and services are module-level functions, so they appear as «module» classifiers. LateDecision is the frozen dataclass returned by evaluate_lateness.
  • Sequence diagrams. Each one traces a single view in code/core/views.py. An alt or opt fragment appears only where that view actually branches. Notes mark behaviour the code does not have, for example that publishing records a reminder as scheduled but sends nothing.

docs.title: Implemented flows without a sequence diagram
docs.text: company_create, round_create, checklist_create and assignment_create are single-form create views (validate, save, write an audit row), and submission_download streams the stored file after an ownership check. These views appear in the class diagram but have no sequence diagram of their own.

docs.title: Not implemented in Week 7 (future work)
docs.text:
These flows are not drawn because they are not in the code:

  • Reminder delivery. Nothing sends a reminder, sets ReminderLog.status to sent or fills in sent_at, and there is no scheduler or background job.
  • Email or any other notification channel.
  • Resubmission. A student can submit once per assignment, enforced by the view and by a database constraint.
  • TA course scoping. Any TA can review or grade any submission.
  • Blocking checklist changes after a round closes. checklist_toggle does not check the round status.

docs.title: Eight UML diagram types
docs.text:
The instructor's announcement specifies eight UML diagrams. This index provides eight distinct UML types, each in its own folder. DFDs, ER diagrams and the Gantt chart are supporting material and are not counted here.

  1. Use-case diagram
  2. Class diagram
  3. Sequence diagram
  4. Activity diagram
  5. State-machine diagram
  6. Component diagram
  7. Deployment diagram
  8. Package diagram

Detailed Week 7 diagrams remain linked from the earlier diagram index. The unchanged submission sequence is shared through relative symlinks. Final use-case, class and activity revisions have their own sources because they document the final ownership and timing guards.
